$comment: Factors behind savings that are NOT measured. scripts/impact-estimates.mjs multiplies a number measured by session-impact.mjs by one of these factors and reports the result apart from measured waste; an estimate is never added into a measured total. `kind` says what a factor stands on: `project-claim` (a number the tool's own project publishes, kept in `quote`), `documented` (behaviour the vendor's documentation describes, kept in `quote`) or `assumption` (no published number exists; `source` states the assumption and `quote` is null). `id` is the stable id printed with each estimate. `label` and `basis` are English; `pt` holds the same two texts in Brazilian Portuguese (`--lang pt`). `basis` is the one sentence printed as the estimate's `source`, with no "source:" prefix: the board adds it. Every entry was checked against its source on `verifiedAt`; entries older than 90 days are re-checked before use. A factor without `source`, `verifiedAt` and `basis` (and a `quote`, unless it is an assumption) is ignored.

estimates.label: Command output a filter would cut
estimates.appliesWhen: The rtk CLI is not installed, according to probe-clis.mjs. When it is installed, or when the probe has no answer, no estimate is made.
estimates.quote: Built by 200+ contributors, written against real command output, and every filter has to cut at least 20% to ship.
estimates.basis: rtk's own README says every filter it ships has to cut at least 20% of a command's output, and that floor is applied here to all the shell output measured in the window: the project's claim, not a measurement.

pt.label: Saída de comandos que um filtro cortaria
pt.basis: O README do próprio rtk diz que todo filtro que ele publica precisa cortar pelo menos 20% da saída de um comando, e esse piso é aplicado aqui a toda a saída de shell medida na janela: é a afirmação do projeto, não uma medição.

caveats: The same README gives the other end of its range as "up to 90% less command output"; the low end is used.
rtk leaves a command it has no filter for untouched, so the floor does not hold for every command head in the window.
The weighted figure counts each token once at the base input rate: command output is input to the model. Cache writes and later re-reads of the same output are not added.

estimates.label: Exploration a knowledge graph could answer
estimates.appliesWhen: Project scope, the project holds code, and it has no graphify-out/ folder. When the snapshot does not say whether the folder exists, no estimate is made.
estimates.source: assumption: a quarter of the exploration before the first edit is structural lookup (where something is defined, what uses it) that a knowledge graph could answer
estimates.basis: Assumption, not a measurement: a quarter of the measured exploration before the first edit is structural lookup that a knowledge graph could answer.

pt.label: Exploração que um grafo de conhecimento poderia responder
pt.basis: Suposição, não medição: um quarto da exploração medida antes da primeira edição é busca estrutural que um grafo de conhecimento poderia responder.

caveats: No published number was found for this share, so none is cited.

The share is kept below one half on purpose: reading the files that are then edited is part of the same measured exploration, and a graph does not replace it. A graph query also costs a model call of its own, which is not subtracted.

estimates.label: Descriptions of skills never invoked
estimates.appliesWhen: A skill listed in unusedContext.skillsNeverInvoked has a descriptionChars in the snapshot's elements.skills.
estimates.base: elements.skills[].descriptionChars, counted as characters / 4, times the sessions in the window
quote: In a regular session, skill descriptions are loaded into context so Claude knows what's available, but full skill content only loads when invoked.
the combined `description` and `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing to reduce context usage.
When the listing overflows, Claude Code drops descriptions starting with the skills you invoke least, so the skills you use most keep their full text.
estimates.basis: Description length of each skill never invoked in the window (capped at 1,536 characters, counted as characters / 4) times the sessions in the window, because Claude Code's documentation says skill descriptions are loaded into context in every session; it is an upper bound, since an overflowing skill listing drops the least-invoked descriptions first.

pt.label: Descrições de skills nunca invocadas
pt.basis: Tamanho da descrição de cada skill nunca invocada na janela (limitado a 1.536 caracteres, contado como caracteres / 4) vezes as sessões da janela, porque a documentação do Claude Code diz que as descrições das skills são carregadas no contexto em toda sessão; é um limite superior, já que uma lista de skills que estoura o orçamento descarta primeiro as descrições das menos invocadas.

caveats: Characters / 4 is the same token approximation session-impact.mjs uses for tool output; it is a convention, not a tokenizer.
The documentation cited is Claude Code's. Whether another agent loads skill descriptions the same way was not checked.
No weighted figure is given: the listing is mostly read from the prompt cache, and how often it is written or read is not measured.

estimates.label: MCP server never called
estimates.appliesWhen: A server is listed in unusedContext.mcpServersNeverCalled.
estimates.basis: Configured, but none of its tools was called in the window; no token number is given because the size of its tool schemas is not in any probe.

pt.label: Servidor MCP nunca chamado
pt.basis: Configurado, mas nenhuma de suas ferramentas foi chamada na janela; não há número de tokens porque o tamanho dos esquemas das ferramentas não aparece em nenhuma sondagem.
